newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood talent agency to set up record label.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood talent agency to set up record label.

text.p: The William Morris Agency, a major Hollywood talent agency, plans to set up its own record label, which would operate as a separate entity.
Details such as a name, staffing and corporate strategy will be ironed out within the next three months, said the agency's chief operating officer Walter Zifkin.
"It seemed like a natural thing that didn't present any conflict issues," he said in an interview on Sunday.
Talent agencies are legally prevented from owning a medium such as a television network or a movie studio, because of the potential conflict of interest arising from handling both ends of the deal.

Musicians are represented in their record deals by managers and attorneys, while talent agencies arrange their touring schedules. Therefore, owning a label would not make the agency both a buyer and a seller of talent. William Morris artists include Pearl Jam and Gloria Estefan.
Nonetheless, William Morris sought approval from the union that represents musicians, the American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (AFTRA).
The group decided at a meeting on Saturday that the new label was "not adverse" to AFTRA members, Zifkin said.

Zifkin said the new label would look to model itself on successful niche players such as Interscope Records, a relative newcomer with a strong roster including No Doubt, Bush and Marilyn Manson. Interscope is half-owned by MCA Music, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.

William Morris is expected to seek outside executives to run the label. Other issues under discussion include whether to buy an existing label or to start one from scratch, and the possibility of equity partners, Zifkin said.

While the music industry has suffered from flat growth in recent years, margins are still better than they are in movies. Zifkin was confident the agency could put together a label that produces "a fair share of winners."
